Everything revealed for Zenless Zone Zero 3.4, including Sunbringer, Kafka, and free Robin
items.summary: Zenless Zone Zero 3.4 introduces Sunbringer, Honkai: Star Rail crossover characters Kafka and Robin, new events, and a free Robin reward for players.
items.content:
All News Zenless Zone Zero’s highly-anticipated Void Hunter is almost here (Image: HoYoverse).

{" "} Everything revealed for Zenless Zone Zero 3.4, including Sunbringer, Kafka, and free Robin .iframe-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .img-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .a-img-media {aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} The Zenless Zone Zero x Honkai: Star Rail crossover launches in December. HoYoverse is officially releasing Version 3.4 of Zenless Zone Zero on 2 December, entitled “The Finality of the Day.” This version update is a chunky one for the game, adding an all-new playable Void Hunter in Sunbringer and two crossover Agents from Honkai: Star Rail: Kafka and Robin.

We’ll break down everything you need to know about this upcoming patch below.

Zenless Zone Zero’s Roscaelifer arc is reaching a climax, following the invasion of High Ambitions Corp. and the Bangboo corruption incident. This time around, Proxies are leaning on powerful allies: the three Sunbringers, Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda, who team up to take on a formidable foe and defend the floating city.

This patch will bring new characters into the fray and reveal what comes next for Zenless Zone Zero Season 3, which has thus far mostly consisted of stories set in Roscaelifer.

Zenless Zone Zero Version 3.4’s headline gacha banner is Sunbringer, the leader of Roscaelifer and ancient Void Hunter. As explained in the game’s lore, Sunbringer has essentially been reborn as three distinct versions of herself: Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda. Hence, players will be able to play as all three in the game, making Sunbringer the game’s first three-in-one Agent. Each of them also have separate Trust Events.

Sunbringer is an S-Rank Genesis Flare Armorer Agent, wielding a lance, greatsword, and shield, with players being able to swap between all three Sunbringers depending on their inputs in combat. Armorer attacks stack Gash on enemies, and consuming Gash will trigger Main and build up Wishfire.

When Sunbringer has enough Wishfire, she can hold basic attack to hurl her lance forward and make her entrance, kicking off a synergy chain attack. She can also enter a two-stage Ultimate that detonates all Embermark stacks on the enemy at once, triggering Emberburst for huge amounts of damage.

Sunbringer will launch as a Signal Search banner with her S-Rank Armorer W-Engine Dragonfire Mirage, along with the new Bangboo Sleepwalkerboo.

That’s not all, however. Zenless Zone Zero is also welcoming two crossover Agents to the roster from Honkai: Star Rail, Robin and Kafka. Both characters use their signature attack styles from the latter turn-based game. Robin (Ether Defense) can keep performing her Concerto off-field, much like Astra Yao, to grant teammates shields while buffing their DEF and DMG, and can re-enter the field to extend these effects. Her Ultimate restores Sharpness for Armorer Agents.

Kafka is an Electric Anomaly Agent who deals damage using Attribute Anomalies and Disorder DMG. In the Hunter’s Overture state, she can either slash and shoot to deal enhanced direct DMG or speed up Attribute Anomaly buildup. Her slashes can also trigger damaging Lightning Surges to Attribute Anomaly-afflicted enemies.

Robin is also getting a new skin called Cosmic Beat at launch. Both Sunbringer and Robin’s Signal Search banners will open at launch and run throughout Version 3.4. However, Kafka will only arrive in Version 3.4’s second half. Alice and her W-Engine Practiced Perfection will rerun in Version 3.4’s second half. Sunbringer is also getting a Moonlit Promenade outfit.

If you’re wondering how Zenless Zone Zero is planning to justify adding in its Honkai: Star Rail characters, wonder no more: the game is adding a “Lost in a Theatrical Dream” collab event in Version 3.4, allowing players to work with Robin and Kafka to film a series together. Through this event, they’ll be able to earn the collab Bangboo Pom-Pom.

Additionally, Robin will be free to claim for any players who log in after Version 3.4 launches. Players will also receive materials to upgrade the W-Engine Twilight Afterimage and all remaining Agent Focus: Pyrois for free. Daily login check-ins will also allow players to claim up to 1,600 Polychromes starting on 1 January.

items.title: Recruit Familiar Faces in the Zenless Zone Zero x Honkai: Star Rail Collab!
How Honkai: Star Rail rejuvenated turn-based RPGs with the feel of action games
items.summary: With the launch of the free-to-play RPG
items.content:
More than three years later, Honkai: Star Rail's possibilities still feel endless

a]:text-inherit [&>a]:underline"> When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: HoYoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Threads Email Instagram Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Hoyoverse made its global breakthrough with the free-to-play open-world action role-playing game (RPG) smash hit Genshin Impact . This was an evolution of its previous mobile hit Honkai Impact 3rd , which for its time was one of the best examples of replicating the smooth, responsive feel of a character action game like Bayonetta with a touchscreen. Following on from these games, Honkai: Star Rail must have felt like such a left-field turn.

Although it carries the Honkai name, this free-to-play RPG was a departure not just in its science-fantasy setting, as you took on the role of the Trailblazer exploring the universe on the space train, the Astral Express, but also in playing as a turn-based RPG.

It's not that this genre has completely fallen out of fashion, when you think of modern classics like 2017's Persona 5 and Square Enix's HD2D releases like Octopath Traveler . Of course, the latter being clearly retro-inspired also reinforces the notion that these games are feeling a bit old hat, with long-standing series like Final Fantasy and even Pokémon making a pivot towards more action-oriented releases.

Yet while Final Fantasy 16 divided fans on its launch in 2023 with a direction that ditched any menu commands for pure action, Honkai: Star Rail 's release in the same year was a huge success, reaching more than 20 million downloads within its first week, and exceeding 100 million downloads by the time of its 2.0 update.

More than three years on, as its 4.7 update releases, TechRadar Gaming had the chance to speak with lead game designer Chengnan An about how this live-service game has joined the likes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 in rejuvenating our love for the turn-based RPG.

Honkai: Nexus Anima could be the free-to-play Pokémon killer A game for those who 'want something high quality' but doesn't reuire players 'to grind, to compete, or to perform' — why the Genshin Impact studio is making a cozy game that prioritises everyday pleasures over daily grinding Cairn and Furi creator’s games are all so different that ‘there’s a chance our next game is an MMO match-3 about friendship,’ jokes creative director, Emeric Thoa Turn on Of course, you can't look back at 2023 without acknowledging Baldur's Gate 3 (which was also TechRadar's game of the year ). Yet while it could be counted as part of the turn-based RPG renaissance, its success can also be attributed to the rising popularity of D&D rather than video games specifically.

" Baldur's Gate 3 is more like a traditional tabletop where you are also playing a role, but it used turn-based combat quite successfully in the tradition of CRPGs, while Honkai: Star Rail is more based on story-driven JRPGs," he says. "Some of my colleagues and I are also big turn-based RPG fans, so we also learn from some classical turn-based games' combat mechanics."

While there's clearly reverence for these older games, it's also not just about repeating the formula but also modernizing it with new twists. One example An gives is the introduction of character ultimate attacks. "As you can use these beyond the common turn order, players can choose to use it immediately or save them for a better moment. This simple design of ultimates gives our players more freedom of control, so they can enjoy the game in an easier way, and still have their own freedom to make options to change the status of the battlefield."

But even as a turn-based RPG, Honkai: Star Rail has also taken inspiration from Honkai Impact 3rd by also injecting some action elements. This is something we have also seen in other first-class modern takes on the genre, from Persona 5 's stylish UI, where every command is also mapped to a different button instead of a menu, to the parry and dodge mechanics in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

Honkai: Star Rail 's secret sauce lies in its characters and, for An, they are "the heart of our game". With each new update adding to the roster, there are always considerations of what unique mechanics they can bring to each character. "When we design characters, we not only want players to feel its visual presentation but also its mechanics," says An. "We want our players to love our characters because of the charm they can feel firsthand in combat."

Stranger Than Heaven preview: all the makings of a unique off-beat adventure from RGG Studio Final Fantasy Resonance review: classic RPG greatness made for 2026 I’m catching up on two of the best time loop games from 2021 For example, Castorice, released in Version 3.2, is a character who can summon a massive dragon to fight alongside her. The team didn't stop at just making this a visually spectacular summon but one that players could also control to some degree when unleashing the dragon's fire breath attacks. But while this was borne from wanting to capture the most exciting ways dragons are usually depicted in media, including The Hobbit and Game of Thrones , An also tells us how the team gave it a modern twist. "It's also inspired by real life, from the acceleration experience of a sports car, when you accelerate from one gear as the engine rises and you switch gears and get more powerful feedback, and so we combine that into the attack rhythm!"

items.title: Razer's Honkai Star Rail collection puts Silver Wolf on a chair, keyboard, mouse and headset
items.summary: Silver Wolf runs this drop. Razer's Honkai Star Rail collection rebuilds four desk staples around her LV.999 hacker look. The set covers a gaming chair, a
items.content:
Silver Wolf runs this drop. Razer’s Honkai Star Rail collection rebuilds four desk staples around her LV.999 hacker look. The set covers a gaming chair, a tenkeyless keyboard, an esports mouse and a wireless headset in her purple and cyan art from the game.

Pre-orders are open at Razer today, and two of the four pieces are already sitting on Amazon at the same prices. Every purchase packs a code for Honkai Star Rail rewards, and the codes stay valid until March 31, 2029.

RazerStores and select retailers get the collection later, with no date attached yet. Canada sits out this pre-order round entirely. Everyone else orders through Razer today. The four pieces share one art style across the desk. Buying one piece on its own still gets you its reward code.

The chair is the Razer Iskur V2 X NewGen in its Honkai Star Rail Edition finish, and the back panel carries a full color portrait of Silver Wolf herself. Flip it around and the front stays much quieter, with her wolf icon sitting above the seat. It’s the loudest piece in the set. Nobody else at the desk will miss it.

Razer Iskur V2 X NewGen – Honkai Star Rail Edition Gen-2 EPU leather with CoolTouch · Built-in lumbar support · 400 Stellar Jade and 20,000 credits included Price: $449.99 at Razer · Standard NewGen $349.99 on Amazon Where to buy: Standard edition Buy on Amazon · Honkai Star Rail Edition Buy at Razer

Under the art, the chair runs Razer’s Gen-2 EPU leather with CoolTouch technology, and the finish is meant to feel cooler across long sessions. Long sessions are the target. The chair is the one piece you see from across the room. It photographs like merch. The back support stays put during long sessions.

The Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed wears pink, white and teal keycaps under the same Silver Wolf treatment, and the tenkeyless frame keeps your mouse hand closer. It connects over 2.4 GHz HyperSpeed wireless or Bluetooth, so one board can jump between a PC and a second device without a cable swap. Razer Chroma RGB lighting runs under every cap on the board.

Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed – Honkai Star Rail Edition Tenkeyless layout · 2.4 GHz HyperSpeed and Bluetooth · Hot swappable switches · Chroma RGB · 250 Stellar Jade included Price: $199.99 Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

The switches are hot swappable, which means you can pull a switch and drop in a different feel without buying a second board. Pink arrow keys finish it. The board keeps a compact footprint on smaller desks. Chroma colors can match the rest of the set. Bluetooth covers the couch sessions.

The Razer Viper V3 Pro SE keeps the lightest hardware in the set at just 54 grams, and the shell wears a dark Silver Wolf graphic across the top. Inside sits Razer’s Focus Pro 35K Optical Sensor Gen-2, paired with HyperSpeed wireless for the connection. The standard black version of this mouse lists 95 hours of battery on Amazon. Her art covers the shell.

Razer Viper V3 Pro SE – Honkai Star Rail Edition 54 g shell · Focus Pro 35K Optical Sensor Gen-2 · HyperSpeed wireless · 100 Stellar Jade included Price: $119.99 at Razer · Standard SE $99.97 on Amazon Where to buy: Standard edition Buy on Amazon · Honkai Star Rail Edition Buy at Razer

Speed is the pitch. A 54 gram mouse moves fast on a big pad, and the sensor tracks flicks without spinning out mid fight, so shooter rounds between story chapters feel snappy.

Power on the Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed and Silver Wolf greets you herself, since the headset plays an exclusive startup voice line from the character. Fans will love that. The hardware underneath stays practical for ranked nights, long calls and late story sessions at the desk at home.

Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed – Honkai Star Rail Edition TriForce 50 mm drivers Gen-2 · Detachable HyperClear mic · Silver Wolf startup voice line · 400 Stellar Jade included Price: $119.99 Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail Still Shows No Sign of XBOX or Switch Launch
items.summary: If you're waiting for Honkai: Star Rail to come to XBOX or Nintendo Switch, you might be waiting just a little while longer...
items.content:
The HoYoverse slate can be pretty hard to keep up with at times. It’s spread across multiple platforms, but differently for each game. In 2024, Genshin Impact arrived on XBOX after four years on the market, and Zenless Zone Zero followed in 2026, two years after launch.

Petit Planet, HoYoverse’s highly anticipated life-sim game that offers players the ability to manage micro-planet-sized environments zipping around a solar system, is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 next year . But Honkai: Star Rail, which dropped in 2023 on mobile and PC and later arrived on PlayStation 5, still shows absolutely no signs of expanding to these platforms.

During a press chat in Seoul, South Korea, Honkai: Star Rail’s lead game designer, Chengen An, spoke at length about the future of the wider HoYoverse. He addressed the ‘ambition’ to bring the game to a wider player base, but admitted there was absolutely nothing to share at that time.

We always want to reach a larger group of players, and we’re always looking into development for different platforms.

There are always pros and cons, like device performance and how profitable it could be, so we always make a comprehensive decision based on the gameplay experience, controls, and technologies.

So far, we don’t have much to share at this point, but please stay tuned to our official announcements.

It’s tactical, to be honest. He doesn’t write the possibility off entirely, and the notion to wait for official announcements might be a nod to something coming soon . But that’s just conjecture.

Are you waiting for Honkai: Star Rail to come to XBOX or Nintendo Switch? Let us know your thoughts on the Insider Gaming Discord server .

For more Insider Gaming coverage, check out our exclusive about Tarkov coming to console , and don’t forget to sign up for our free weekly newsletter

Grant has been gaming for 30+ years and in the industry for 10+. You'll probably find him playing a post-apocalyptic game or an extraction shooter somewhere.

items.title: Honkai Star Rail’s First Playable Aeon Isn’t A Damage God, And That’s A Good Thing
Razer Powers Up Its Play With Honkai: Star Rail Collaboration
items.summary: Razer has teamed up with HoYoverse for another hardware collaboration, this time based on their popular gacha RPG: Honkai Star Rail.
items.content:
Add us on Google Since its launch in 2023, Honkai: Star Rail has captivated gamers with its interesting story and unique gacha-style gameplay. Now, Razer is partnering with HoYoverse for another exclusive line of gamer gear based on the RPG.

Announced via press release, following previous collaborations with Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero , the Razer | Honkai: Star Rail Collection is inspired by Silver Wolf LV.999, the invincible player from the game. The gaming hardware, with her unmistakable aesthetic and competitive spirit, will be comprised of a premium gaming chair, mouse, keyboard and headset aptly named the “Ctrl + Alt + WIN” collection.

“”From Genshin Impact to Zenless Zone Zero and now Honkai: Star Rail , this collaboration is a tribute to the communities that have made these worlds so beloved,” said Global Head of Lifestyle Division at Razer, Addie Tan. She continued, “Silver Wolf’s LV.999 mastery reflects Razer’s ethos of performance-driven, cutting-edge design, and we’re proud to bring her genius hacker style into the physical realm, giving players and fans a new way to experience the game beyond the screen.”

According to the release, the Razer Iskur V2 X NewGen – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is built with long-lasting ergonomic support and all-day comfort for players who know every session is another chance to level up. The Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition combines ultra-low-latency Razer HyperSpeed Wireless performance with a compact tenkeyless layout and Razer Chroma RGB for a keyboard that is responsive and ready for any game.

The Razer Viper V3 Pro SE – Honkai: Star Rail Edition was inspired by Silver Wolf’s LV.999 gaming instincts; this ultra-lightweight wireless esports mouse delivers uncompromising speed and precision. The Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is tournament-ready wireless audio with lightweight comfort; this headset gives players the competitive edge every match demands. What’s more, every time players turn on their headset, they’ll be greeted with an exclusive startup voice line from Silver Wolf.

The Razer Iskur V2 X NewGen will retail for $449.99 USD, the Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed for $199.99 USD, while the Razer Viper V3 Pro S and the Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed will cost $119.99 USD, with every purchase also including Honkai: Star Rail in-game rewards. No release date was provided for this new collection; however, all items are available for pre-order globally (excluding Canada) on the official Razer website .

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.7 "Now, Lay Laughter to All Stars" Begins on November 11
Honkai: Star Rail Dev Explains Aha & Discusses Future Playable Aeons
items.summary: Aha might be just the start of what's to come.
items.content:
Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Ben Brosofsky Published Nov 8, 2026, 8:00 PM EST Ben Brosofsky has been writing for Screen Rant since 2022 and editing since 2024. He graduated from Vanderbilt University with a Bachelor's in Cinema & Media Arts. Writing serves as a much-needed distraction from tackling a backlog of Steam games that will never be surmounted. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Genshin Impact brought the world of HoYoverse games to a much larger audience than ever before, but Honkai: Star Rail was the game that proved the company's staying power. Several years later, Star Rail is still going strong, even after the launch of Zenless Zone Zero and the impending release of games like Petit Planet and Honkai: Nexus Anima .

At a HoYoverse press event in Seoul, ScreenRant sat down in a group interview with Honkai: Star Rail 's lead game designer Chengnan An to discuss the state of the game and future plans. Honkai: Star Rail 's introduction of the first playable Aeon, Aha, naturally came up in the conversation, and the developers offered some details about both Aha's development and the potential for future playable Aeons.

First, Chengnan An addressed the tricky subject of making an Aeon playable in combat without upsetting the balance. While power creep always tends to come into the conversation with ongoing live-service games, HoYoverse doesn't want to simply drop an Aeon into the mix and " overcome all the existing characters ." In Aha's case, focusing purely on destructive strength would also fail to " fit her personality as an Aeon of Elation ."

Aha was chosen as the first playable Aeon due to her status as " the most human-like one ," making her a less " abstract concept " to most people in Honkai: Star Rail 's world than other Aeons might be. That being said, it doesn't sound like other Aeons are off the table at all in future updates. " When we design different Aeons , there would also be different ways to showcase them ."

As for the nature of Aha's role in-game, An established that the plan was always for her to be a support character, as " Aha is closely connected to other characters ." Ultimately, " Path of Elation is also about bringing happiness and all these emotions ," so having Aha focus on dealing damage might not have fit the bill quite as well.

An didn't offer any teases about which Aeons might have the potential to become playable in the future, but the community can probably guess at the subject with a reasonable amount of expertise. Nous might be the prime possibility, as the idea of Nous taking on a human form has been hinted at previously. There's also plenty of speculation around theoretical reveals of the Trailblazer and other primary characters ascending as Aeons, which could open another can of worms.

Regardless, the introduction of Aha is more than enough for players to worry about at the moment. The Aeon is set to debut with the Honkai: Star Rail 4.7 update on November 11, 2026, so there isn't long to wait now until the Path of Elation truly unfolds. Beyond that, fans will just have to wait and see what the future plans for other Aeons in Honkai: Star Rail might be.
